title: Tool-call manifest format, strictness tiers, and diagnostic payload design
creator: Lena Brooks
description: Define a compact, implementation-friendly JSON manifest for tool/function calls that encodes parameter types, optional strictness tiers, and a machine-friendly diagnostic payload for runtime validation errors. This ticket captures the authoring format, runtime mapping, error contract, and a rollout/migration plan to replace ad-hoc schema blobs currently used by multiple services.
background: We currently have multiple incompatible ad-hoc JSON blobs used to describe tool parameters across hosted, dedicated, and private runtimes. These variations cause inconsistent validation behavior, noisy user-facing error messages, and friction during model->tool compatibility upgrades. Existing documents cover parts of the problem (validation, compatibility, error taxonomies) but none prescribe a single manifest shape plus strictness semantics and a diagnostic payload that pods can emit and the Console can surface consistently.
proposal_summary: Introduce a 'tool manifest' JSON format (v2) with: a concise parameter table, an explicit 'strictness' enum per parameter and per-call default, canonical coercion rules, and a standardized error diagnostic object (code, path, severity, hint, docs_url, i18n_key). Define runtime behavior for three strictness tiers (relaxed, warn, strict). The runtime will map legacy blobs to the manifest shape via a compatibility adapter and emit diagnostics in the new contract. Console and SDKs will translate diagnostics into localized messages and suggested fixes.
schema_format: Manifest v2 is deliberately compact: top-level keys: 'id', 'version', 'description', 'parameters' (array of parameter objects), 'defaults' (optional), 'strictness' (optional default). Each parameter object: 'name', 'type' (string, number, boolean, object, array, enum), 'required' (boolean), 'strictness' (inherit from top-level if absent), 'coercion' (none|string_to_number|split_csv|json_parse), 'examples' (array of short strings), 'deprecated_in' (optional version tag). No nested schema trees — nested objects are allowed but described via 'shape_id' referencing an inline shape list to keep authoring small and human-readable.
strictness_levels: relaxed: best-effort coercion, validation errors downgraded to diagnostics with severity 'info' and call proceeds
warn: attempt coercion, emit diagnostic with severity 'warning' and continue; if coercion fails emit 'warning' diagnostic and drop parameter to default if available
strict: validation failure is treated as error (HTTP 4xx), call rejected; runtime emits diagnostic with severity 'error' and canonical code
error_contract: Diagnostics emitted by the runtime MUST be an array of diagnostic objects. Diagnostic fields: 'code' (short machine string, e.g., 'param.type_mismatch'), 'message' (English fallback), 'i18n_key' (translation key), 'path' (JSON path to parameter), 'severity' (info|warning|error), 'hint' (short user-facing remediation suggestion), 'docs_url' (link to param docs), 'suggested_value' (string example or canonicalized value if available). All diagnostics are idempotent and stable across replays.
runtime_behavior: Runtimes will implement a compatibility adapter to read legacy schemas and produce a manifest v2 projection. During validation, coercion rules are applied in order: canonicalization -> coercion -> custom validator. Diagnostics are emitted at each phase. For strictness=relaxed the runtime attaches diagnostics but does not fail the call; for strictness=warn it returns 200 with diagnostics in response metadata; for strictness=strict it returns 4xx and includes diagnostics in the error body. SDKs will expose diagnostics via a typed Diagnostics object and Console will render them with translation and 'apply suggestion' quick actions when 'suggested_value' exists.
compatibility_strategy: Phase 1: Accept legacy blobs and emit manifest-equivalent diagnostics without changing call surface. Phase 2: Offer an opt-in manifest authoring UI and CLI linter. Phase 3: Default to manifest v2 for new tool registrations; older tools will be left in compatibility mode for 6 months, with metrics collected on diagnostics surface. Provide an automated migration tool to convert common legacy patterns to manifest v2 where possible.
migration_notes: We will run a non-blocking migration in runtime-1.20 behind a feature flag. The adapter will generate diagnostics tagged 'compat.migration' so we can measure prevalence. Migration tool will create draft manifests in a customer-visible queue for admin approval in Console. Rollback plan: feature flag off reverts to legacy validation.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest v2 schema documented in runtime docs and a JSON schema provided for authoring
Runtime compatibility adapter implemented and covered by integration tests (>=80% coverage for adapter flows)
SDKs expose Diagnostics objects and can localize messages using i18n_key
Console surfaces diagnostics with severity coloring and quick-suggest actions for at least three common coercions
Migration tool can auto-convert >=70% of legacy tool manifests in dataset sample and queue remaining for manual review
implementation_steps: Design doc merged with examples and conversion rules
Minimal JSON Schema for manifest v2 and generator script (runtime team)
Compatibility adapter implementation in serving runtime and validation integration tests
SDK changes: Diagnostics type + translation hooks (JS/Go/Python)
Console changes: diagnostic renderer + migration queue UI
Migration tool and a small pilot customer group
rollout_plan: Week 0: Feature flag gated deployment to staging; run conversion tool against internal manifests
Week 2: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for non-critical customers; collect diagnostics metrics
Week 4: Expand to 50% and enable SDK beta with Diagnostics API
Week 8: Opt-in Console migration flow for customers; begin auto-convert suggestions
Week 12: Default new registrations to manifest v2; legacy compatibility remains for 6 months
